$comment: Single source of truth for what a pdfe-windows self-hosted runner needs.
BOTH Install-PdfeRunner.ps1 and Test-PdfeRunner.ps1 read this file, so a
dependency cannot be installed-but-unverified or verified-but-uninstalled.
Two separate hand-maintained lists is how a runner ends up missing a tool
that the installer 'handles' -- which is literally the OpenCppCoverage
situation this package exists to fix.
Every entry names the WORKFLOW STEP that consumes it, so a future reader
can tell whether an item is still needed without guessing.
NO WINGET. Four entries here used to say kind:'winget'. That does not work
on the machines this package targets: the existing runner is Windows Server
2019, which has no Microsoft Store, and winget ships as the App Installer
Store package. Measured on the live host -- winget is absent AND the Appx
module fails to load at all ('Operation is not supported on this platform'),
so App Installer cannot be added either. winget was not a fallback away from
working; it was unreachable by construction.
Everything installable is therefore kind:'download' -- an explicit pinned
URL plus explicit silent_args. ONE code path, exercised on every machine,
including ones that do have winget. Silent args are DATA here rather than
inferred from the file extension, because the inference was wrong: Git is
Inno Setup (/VERYSILENT), OpenCppCoverage is NSIS (/S), and the Visual
Studio bootstrapper is neither.
PROFILES: each requirement carries the profiles it belongs to, so a profile cannot drift out of sync with the requirement list the way a separate hand-maintained roster would.
_target_labels_note: These are the labels a DEFAULT (solo) deployment must register with, and
they now include `pdfe-builder`. They previously did not, which made every
machine provisioned by this package unable to run windows-validation's
`build` and `release` jobs -- those two are the only ones whose `runs-on`
carries `pdfe-builder`. GitHub does not error on an unsatisfiable
`runs-on`: the job QUEUES and is then reported `cancelled`, a status
indistinguishable from a deliberate cancellation and one that alerts
nobody. So the symptom of the old default was silence.
THE FLEET MUST DEGRADE TO ONE MACHINE. Other runners (the ephemeral
Hetzner box, any second Windows machine) are not always present, and their
absence must never fail anything -- the work simply lands here instead.
That is only true if the machine that IS present carries every label the
workflows ask for, which is what this list now guarantees.
See `profiles.consume` below for the one case where a NARROWER label set is
correct, and why it must never be a solo machine's profile.

requirements.name: Windows 10/11 or Server 2019+ x64
requirements.why: All five workflows are runs-on: [self-hosted, Windows, X64, pdfe-windows].

requirements.name: Interactive desktop session (NOT a Windows service)
requirements.why: The UI E2E suite drives a real PDFE.exe window through UIA (pywinauto/WinAppDriver). UIA needs a real desktop; a service-mode runner in session 0 has no visible desktop and every UI test blinds or hangs. This is why the existing runner is run.cmd rather than a service -- see docs/audit and the ui_pytest_requires_bash_shell note.
requirements.tension: A service would survive reboots and not die silently, which is the OTHER known failure (selfhosted_runner_ops: run.cmd dies silently, unserviced runs queue then report cancelled). These two requirements genuinely conflict. Resolution used here: interactive session + autologon + the watchdog in Watch-PdfeRunner.ps1, NOT a service.

requirements.name: Git for Windows
requirements.why: actions/checkout on a self-hosted runner uses the system git. Floor is 2.18 because that is what actions/checkout documents needing (sparse-checkout/submodule paths); an earlier draft of this file said 2.40 with no basis and failed a working machine running 2.30 -- an invented requirement is as bad as a missing one.

install.note: Inno Setup, so /VERYSILENT -- NOT /S, which Inno ignores and which would leave an interactive installer waiting forever on a headless deploy. /o:PathOption=Cmd is what puts git on the machine PATH; without it actions/checkout cannot find it.

requirements.name: Visual Studio 2022 with the C++ desktop workload
requirements.why: MSVC toolchain for the windows-vs2022 preset. CMakePresets.json hard-codes the VS-bundled Ninja at 'C:/Program Files/Microsoft Visual Studio/2022/Community/Common7/IDE/CommonExtensions/Microsoft/CMake/Ninja/ninja.exe', so the COMMUNITY edition path is what the presets expect.

install.note: Large (~10 GB) and slow; --wait means this call blocks for the whole install. This is the ONE url here that is not version-pinned -- aka.ms/vs/17/release always resolves to current VS 2022, and Microsoft publishes no stable per-version bootstrapper URL. If a VS edition other than Community is installed, CMakePresets.json's hard-coded Ninja path will NOT resolve -- see the README.

requirements.name: CMake 3.31+
requirements.why: Project requires 3.31+ in manifest mode. The VS-bundled CMake satisfies this and is what the project documents using.

requirements.name: Python 3.11+ with pip
requirements.why: tests/scripts/run_gtest.py (sharded runner), tests/scripts/run_ui_suite.py (UI sweep), the security ctest entries (three of five are python -m pytest), and every tools/gate/*.py checker.

install.note: InstallAllUsers=1 + PrependPath=1 are both required: the runner service account and the interactive operator must resolve the same python, and pip-requirements below shells out to it in the same session.

requirements.name: Pinned UI test dependencies (33 hash-locked packages)
requirements.why: pywinauto / pyautogui / Pillow / pytest and friends for the UI E2E suite. The workflow installs these itself, but pre-installing makes a cold runner's first job much faster and surfaces a broken pip environment at deploy time instead of 90 minutes into a run.

requirements.name: vcpkg (manifest mode)
requirements.why: Every dependency (Qt 6.10, MuPDF, QPDF, Tesseract, ONNX...) comes from vcpkg manifest mode. VCPKG_ROOT must be set for CMakePresets.json's toolchain file to resolve.

requirements.name: OpenCppCoverage
requirements.why: windows-validation.yml step 'Code coverage (OpenCppCoverage -> Cobertura)' treats ABSENCE AS A HARD ERROR (R-32) -- it is a required runner dependency, not optional. The workflow's fallback tries Chocolatey, which is broken on the current runner; that is exactly the failure phase-24 criterion 3 exists to fix. This package installs from the GitHub release MSI instead.

portable_fallback.why: OpenCppCoverage ships ONLY as an Inno installer, which requires elevation -- and a runner account is often not in the local Administrators group, making the install an operator action that may never happen. It does not need installing: the payload extracts with innoextract and runs standalone, because it instruments via the debugging APIs, which work for a same-user process. Verified on the live runner from an unelevated extracted copy: a real Cobertura report, lines-valid=53399. Extracting to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs and adding that to the USER PATH needs no elevation at all. windows-validation.yml checks this location FIRST.

install.note: INNO SETUP, not NSIS. An earlier version of this file asserted NSIS and passed /S; the downloaded bytes say otherwise (3 'Inno Setup' signature hits, 0 NSIS). This matters more than a mislabel: Inno IGNORES unrecognised switches and falls back to its INTERACTIVE wizard, so /S under Start-Process -Wait hangs forever on a headless runner rather than failing. Deliberately NOT choco -- choco is the path that is broken on the current runner -- and NOT winget, which is unreachable on Server 2019.

requirements.name: WinAppDriver >= 1.2.1
requirements.why: WAD-driven UI tests. Below 1.2.1 the 2016 v0 beta answers /status but cannot create sessions (PDFE-LIMITATION-WINAPPDRIVER-V0), so a too-old install is worse than none.

requirements.name: Windows Developer Mode enabled
requirements.why: WinAppDriver refuses to start sessions unless Developer Mode is on.

requirements.name: GitHub CLI
requirements.why: Not needed by the workflows themselves, but every operational procedure in this repo uses gh to inspect runs (and gh is NOT on PATH on the current runner -- it lives at C:\Users\dev\bin\gh, which has cost time before).

install.note: Also the escape hatch for Bootstrap-PdfeRunner.ps1 on a machine with neither gh nor a token: this URL is PUBLIC and needs no authentication, whereas the package it fetches does.
Requires a registration token, which is short-lived and must be supplied by a human -- this package will not attempt to obtain one.

requirements.name: Win32 long paths enabled
requirements.why: vcpkg buildtrees plus Qt's deep header layout exceed MAX_PATH on a default Windows install; the symptom is a confusing mid-build file-not-found rather than an obvious path error.

requirements.name: >= 120 GB free (build) / >= 15 GB free (consume)
requirements.why: BUILD profile: vcpkg_installed + buildtrees + two build configs + the ~44 MB ONNX model + artifacts. A cold vcpkg build spikes into the tens of GB transiently, and that PEAK -- not the steady state -- is what 120 GB absorbs. Disk exhaustion on this project has previously presented as an unrelated failure (see vs_diaghub_etw_leak). CONSUME profile: no toolchain at all. Measured on the live host: VS2022 12 GB, vcpkg repo ~2.7 GB, its caches 2.4 GB -- none of it needed. What remains is the ~2.3 GB restored runtime closure plus Python/WinAppDriver/runner, about 5 GB. 15 GB is that with headroom for a second commit's store and log/temp churn.

requirements.name: AWS CLI v2 (S3-compatible client for Cloudflare R2)
requirements.why: The build-closure restore and the crash-dump shipper both shell out to `aws s3`. R2 is S3-compatible and this is the client. WITHOUT IT a consume-only machine cannot obtain binaries at all -- ensure-build-tree reaches its cold-machine refusal and the job fails -- and a build machine cannot publish, so every OTHER machine then fails. It is required on both profiles for opposite reasons: consumers read, builders write. The action fails LOUDLY when R2 is configured and this is absent rather than silently falling through, so the symptom is at least honest; this requirement is what stops it arising.

install.note: Windows Installer package. silent_args is EMPTY because Install-FromUrl drives `msiexec /quiet /norestart` itself for the msi family -- passing them here duplicates the switches and mismatches the convention winappdriver and gh already follow. Caught by Test-InstallerUrls.ps1, which is the same check that found OpenCppCoverage was Inno and not NSIS. Pinned rather than the floating AWSCLIV2.msi so two machines provisioned a week apart cannot silently get different clients.

requirements.name: Cloudflare R2 credentials (machine-level environment)
requirements.why: PDFE_R2_ENDPOINT / PDFE_R2_BUCKET / PDFE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / PDFE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, set at MACHINE scope. Deliberately not workflow secrets: on a self-hosted runner the machine is the trust boundary, and workflow secrets are readable by every job in the repository. This requirement is NOT installable -- credentials are operator-supplied and a script that minted or stored them would be holding something it has no business holding. See docs/ci/r2-build-store.md. Consume-only machines should hold a READ-ONLY token; that is the control the store's integrity rests on.

build.description: THE DEFAULT, and the only correct profile for a machine that is on its own. Compiles pdfe; needs the full MSVC + vcpkg toolchain. windows-validation's `build` and `release` jobs target `pdfe-builder`, so at least ONE machine must carry this profile or those two queue forever and report `cancelled`. When the fleet is a single machine -- which is the normal resting state here, because the other private runners are not always accessible -- that machine must be this profile, so that every self-hosted Windows job in the tree can land on it.

consume.description: OPT-IN, MULTI-MACHINE FLEETS ONLY. NEVER the profile of a solo machine. Runs tests against binaries built elsewhere and restored via the cross-machine build store. It deliberately does NOT carry `pdfe-builder` so GitHub will never route a build job to a machine that cannot build -- a job that lands on the wrong machine does not fail fast, it fails deep into a compile. That reasoning is correct ONLY when some OTHER registered machine carries `pdfe-builder`. Applied to the sole runner it inverts: `build` and `release` become unsatisfiable and die silently in the queue. Choose this profile only when you can name the machine that is carrying the build profile instead.

_consolidation_risk: WHAT SINGLE-MACHINE CONSOLIDATION ACTUALLY PUTS TOGETHER, and why it is accepted.
Adding `pdfe-builder` to the default label set is not only a convenience fix. It
is the change that makes `build` and `release` LAND on the shared host for the
first time -- before it, those two jobs could not be scheduled onto a machine
this package provisioned at all: they queued and were reported `cancelled`. So
the co-location described below did not previously happen in practice, and now
does, by design, because the fleet must degrade to one machine.
CO-LOCATED, IN SERIAL (never concurrent -- every workflow is
`workflow_dispatch`-only and the runner is single-capacity):
* `build` / `release`, which compile and produce published artifacts, and
* `fuzz`, `windows-sanitizer`, `mutation-kill`, `governance`, which build and
execute attacker-shaped PDF input under instrumentation,
on the same host, the same workspace root, and the same machine-scoped
environment that carries PDFE_R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID / PDFE_R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.
WHY IT IS ACCEPTED:
1. `TRUSTED_SIGNING_*` is NEVER touched by CI. `scripts/sign/Sign-Artifacts.ps1`
is not invoked by any workflow -- verified by grep over .github/workflows --
and is a manual, `az login`-first, local-only tool. Release SIGNING
credentials are therefore not present on the runner at all.
2. `PDFE_R2_*` is a BUILD-CACHE credential, not a signing credential, and it is
deliberately machine-scoped: the machine is the trust boundary, and workflow
secrets would be worse, being readable by every job in every workflow. That
rationale predates this change; what is new is that `release` is now one of
the jobs on that boundary. Consume-only machines still hold READ-ONLY,
bucket-scoped tokens.
3. `build` checks out with actions/checkout's DEFAULT `clean: true`
(`git clean -ffdx`), so the producing lane wipes gitignored leftovers at the
start of every run. `clean: false` appears only on jobs downstream of `build`
WITHIN THE SAME RUN, so it does not carry fuzz or sanitizer state across into
a later release build.
RESIDUAL, NOT COVERED BY THE ABOVE -- recorded rather than implied:
* DISK CONTENTION is an availability risk, not an integrity one: a fuzz corpus
or an ASan build can starve a later `release` of space on a host that is
already near its floor. This is the concrete reason the `build` profile asks
for 120 GB free rather than the consume profile's 15.
* NON-REPO-TREE STATE that `git clean -ffdx` cannot reach -- %TEMP%, the local
per-SHA build store, orphaned processes holding the machine-global
single-instance mutex -- survives between lanes on a shared host.
If you have more than one machine, `profiles.consume` exists precisely so you do
not have to accept any of this; see its description.
